pages.text: Most TFMG machines ask for a steel mechanism. It is a $(item)sequenced assembly$() that starts from a $(item)heavy plate$(), with four $(item)deployer$() steps, in this order:

$(li)1. a $(item)steel ingot$()$(li)2. an $(item)aluminium ingot$()$(li)3. $(item)screws$()$(li)4. the $(item)screwdriver$() (worn, not consumed)$(br2)One pass is enough. The result is a $(item)steel mechanism 80%$() of the time, and an $(item)iron nugget$() otherwise.

$(l)A simple line$()$(br)A belt carries heavy plates under four deployers in a row, each holding one of the items above. Keep the first three deployers stocked with funnels or chutes, and give the last one a screwdriver.
Per mechanism, on average: 1 heavy plate, 1 steel ingot, 1 aluminium ingot and 1 screw, divided by 0.8. Count about $(item)1.25 of each$() and $(item)2.5 steel ingots$() in total, plate included.
The items this page talks about. Hover for details; JEI shows their recipes.
